title: Change-aware eval scorecard with chained alert suppression and triage playbook
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Build a change-aware eval scorecard and integrated triage workflow in the Console that links config/model changes to quality regressions, reduces noisy duplicate alerts across channels (Slack/PagerDuty), and surfaces rollback suggestions and runbook steps. The goal is to make it fast for product and on-call engineers to understand whether a regression is caused by a recent config tweak, model swap, or external data drift and to route a single canonical incident with contextualized playbook actions.
background: Our current eval alerts flood channels when multiple signals from the same underlying change fire. Engineers spend time correlating open tickets and duplicate PagerDuty pages.
Existing docs and tickets focus on dedupe and routing, but we lack a unified scorecard that attributes regressions to config/model deltas and proposes next actions (rollback, runbook, link to PR).
Customers operating production workloads want fewer false positives and clearer remediation steps tied to the last deploy/config change.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a per-change eval scorecard: baseline metrics, delta over last deploy/config change, sample failing prompts, and confidence attribution (model|config|data).
Alerting pipeline groups related eval signals into one canonical incident with dedupe rules, with one PagerDuty page per root-cause cluster and one Slack thread for triage comments.

Scorecard surfaces proposed mitigations: rollback model to previous version, apply suggested quantization profile, revert recent batching change, or run specific eval suite; each action links to the relevant PR/rollout and has a one-click 'Create Incident' / 'Acknowledge' action.
Dedupe logic uses a configurable temporal window (default 30 minutes) and causal keys (model_id, config_hash, change_id) to avoid duplicate notifications across channels.
API endpoints documented: GET /evals/changes/:change_id/scorecard, POST /evals/changes/:change_id/actions (rollback, mute, open-incident).
Telemetry emitted for every grouped incident: group_id, root_cause_tag, number_of_signals, channels_notified, resolution_action, time_to_ack, time_to_resolution.
Unit and integration tests covering grouping logic, Slack/PagerDuty payloads, and UI rendering for low/medium/high confidence attributions.
Pilot rollout to internal Platform and one external beta customer with a feedback loop and opt-in flag.
notes: Design kickoff: need heatmap and scorecard mockups from design by 2025-06-25.
Backend: ENG to propose schema for 'change' object that ties config hash, commit, and model version; estimate 3 sprints.
We should reuse existing eval metric thresholds, but introduce a soft-confidence layer to avoid hard-firing on noisy signals.
Consider integrating with existing 'eval-change-correlator' work to seed attribution heuristics.
Privacy: ensure sample prompts scrub PII before embedding into Slack/PagerDuty messages.

review_feedback: From Alex Martinez (Eng): Prefer server-side grouping to minimize duplicate Slack messages; client only displays grouped result. Will add retry/debounce.
From Priya Desai (SRE): PagerDuty grouping must honor on-call owner mapping by team and include 'noisy' suppression mode for low-severity regressions.
From Design (Renee Park): Recommend a 'confidence ribbon' using three colors and inline explanations for attribution heuristics.
From Customer Success (Owen Hall): Beta customers asked for the ability to pin a failing prompt to an existing customer ticket to speed investigation.
open_questions: What is the canonical 'change_id' — commit SHA, infra change ticket, or a combined hash? (ENG to propose schema).
How to surface multi-change incidents where two independent changes coincide and jointly cause regression?
Should rollback actions be automated (one-click) or create a runbook task for operator approval?
Do we require a retention policy for sample prompts beyond 30 days?
